summary:
Second scenario check (action=check) for the already-accepted requirement unit-claim-client-future-shutdown-escape, executing the exposure previously characterised from source; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Design: plan_c9.json plus harness_verify_test.go build a node with background goroutines disabled, call VerifyLeader so the request is accepted into its library-buffered channel (capacity 64), then call Shutdown and probe the returned future without blocking — recording whether a response is available, whether the future carries the shutdown escape, and the derived caller_can_complete. Declarative prerequisite: request_accepted true. Monitor applicability: request_accepted true. Property: an accepted verify request has a completion path, identity op_id, evaluated from emitted fields rather than tests_passed. A control on a served single-node cluster performs the same call and completes.

Construction evidence (not the formal observation): a local run in a copy of the captured module shows caller_can_complete false with responded_after_shutdown false and shutdown_escape false for VerifyLeader, while the served control reports completed true — so the gap is not specific to Apply, and no extra configuration is needed because the library buffers that channel itself.

Declared adaptations: skipStartup makes an accepted-then-dropped request deterministic instead of race-dependent; the probe reads the future's own fields rather than calling Error(), which would block. Retained uncertainties: whether the remaining future types (configurationChangeFuture, bootstrapFuture, userSnapshotFuture, leadershipTransferFuture) share the gap — their unbuffered or single-slot channels narrow the window but do not by themselves remove it — and whether completion after Shutdown is deliberately not guaranteed, in which case the correct disposition is a documented caveat. No target code was modified; fresh execution plus a checker-correspondence review still remain.
